newsitem.title: USA: Berkshire Hathaway to buy Star Furniture.
newsitem.headline: Berkshire Hathaway to buy Star Furniture.

text.p: Warren Buffett is buying another furniture retailer, Star Furniture Co., adding to one of the mainstays at his Berkshire Hathaway Inc. holding company, Star said Tuesday.
Terms of the acquisition were not disclosed.
Closely held Star is the 32nd largest furniture retailer in the nation, according to the industry publication Furniture Today, Star said.

Founded in 1912, it has been run by the Wolff and Toomim families for nearly all of its 85-year history. Star Chairman Melvyn Wolff, Vice Chairman Shirley Toomim and other managers will be retained, as is typical in a Buffett acquisition.
Buffett, one of the nation's most widely followed investors, and Wolff announced the deal at a breakfast held at a convention centre in Houston, the company said.

"We couldn't be more pleased than to have the opportunity to become a part of what we believe to be the finest family of companies ever assembled under one corporate name," Wolff said in a statement. "Warren Buffett has demonstrated a legendary track record for growth and we want to be a part of it."

Star joins the Nebraska Furniture Mart and R.C. Willey, two other furniture and home furnishing retailers owned by Berkshire, which is based in Omaha, Neb. Combined sales for the three retailers are about $684 million, Star said.
Berkshire Hathaway Class A stock, the most expensive on the New York Stock Exchange, rose $300 to $47,700 a share. Its Class B stock added $20 to $1,595, also on the NYSE.
